entries.title: Test database port refuses connections
entries.root_cause: The test configuration points to port 5433, while PostgreSQL is published on port 5432. Correct the test database port.

entries.title: Test database port still refuses connections
entries.root_cause: The test configuration points to port 5433, while PostgreSQL is published on port 5432. Correct the test database port.
entries.differs_from_earlier: A later run uses a different runner and test selection, but retains the same mismatched port.

entries.title: Test database rejects the configured role
entries.root_cause: The test process uses the sluice_reader role with a password that does not match the PostgreSQL service configuration. Align the test role password with the service.
entries.differs_from_earlier: The server is reached on the published port; it rejects the configured role's password instead of refusing a TCP connection.

entries.title: Test database again rejects the configured role
entries.root_cause: The test process uses the sluice_reader role with a password that does not match the PostgreSQL service configuration. Align the test role password with the service.
entries.differs_from_earlier: A later run executes another test and reports the same role authentication failure through a different stack location.
